transcript: alright so here's the deal there's an extremely niche group of people who are gonna go absolutely nuts when they find out this play exists is this video gonna reach that niche? I don't know we're gonna find out so if you're familiar with the Academy Award nominated masterpiece Past Lives you might know that the writer director Celine Song is also a playwright but you almost certainly didn't know about this very obscure early play of hers called Family which is like a psychological horror play and it's being performed as a site specific production in this apartment in Brooklyn for a very intimate audience of like I think less than 30 people and the play is so obscure in fact that I was having trouble finding any information about it online and so when I was at the show tonight I saw Celine song herself in the audience and I asked her about the origins of the play and she told me that she wrote it 10 years ago as her grad school final and it hasn't been performed since then The play is basically about three siblings who are kind of going crazy inside their late father's home but both the family and the house itself have some disturbing twisted mysteries that unfold over the course of the play The whole thing is extremely weird and experimental and it definitely will not be for everybody I will say there is a very dark humor that runs throughout the play which I found very enjoyable but I'm not gonna pretend that it's a particularly easy watch there is a kind of relentless dare I say punishing quality to it but for the most part it worked for me I was very much on the edge of my seat and some parts of it were actually quite chilling so if the content sounds like it might be up your alley and if you like cool intimate site-specific theater and you're excited by this rare opportunity to see an obscure early work from this acclaimed writer then I definitely recommend checking this out. and on that last point it's also worth noting that Celine Song has said in interviews that she wants to focus on film instead of theater for the foreseeable future so like who knows when will get the chance to see another one of her plays in New York? especially one that is more or less a professional premiere so this production is by the company Hoi Polloi and it's running through October 4th
